title: Model Fragility & Recovery Playbook: enterprise availability simulation and competitive mapping
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Purpose: Produce a repeatable playbook and artifact set to quantify model availability risk, simulate vendor outages and performance degradations, and recommend narrow fallback strategies for enterprise customers. Scope: competitive mapping of model vendors + community models across availability, latency, cost volatility, and degradation modes (API rate limits, version deprecations, quantized-quality shifts, regional supply constraints). Deliverables: 1) model fragility taxonomy, 2) interactive availability heatmap by region/model, 3) two outage simulation runbooks with measurable KPIs, 4) recommended default fallback chains and rollout policy templates for Console. Success metrics: playbook reviewed and accepted by Solutions and GTM; two simulated outages executed in staging with verified automatic fallbacks; identification of top-3 vendor risks and concrete mitigations for Dedicated and Private offerings.
acceptance_criteria: Fragility taxonomy documented and linked in Confluence
Interactive heatmap (region x vendor x failure-mode) available and validated against historical incidents
Two staged outage simulations completed in staging with telemetry captured and postmortem written
Fallback chains (primary -> secondary -> degraded-mode) defined for top 6 enterprise-in-use models and encoded as rollout policy templates
Stakeholder signoff from Solutions, SRE, and Legal on proposed mitigations and customer communication templates
steps: Inventory current model usage across top 50 enterprise accounts (embeddings/generation/reranking) via Billing/Console exports
Define failure-mode matrix with Engineering and SRE (API outage, rate-limit throttling, model-accuracy regression, region-specific unavailability, pricing spike, data-residency loss)
Map known vendor constraints (rate limits, regional coverage, SLA language) into the heatmap data model
Produce simulated outage harness (k8s job + traffic shaping) to emulate 1) total vendor outage and 2) quality degradation via forced quantized paths
Run simulations in staging with Canary accounts and collect latency, error-rate, quality-degradation metrics (BLEU/ROUGE proxies for regression where applicable and embedding-similarity drift)
Synthesize fallback policies: automatic routing to pinned compatible model, best-effort quantized variant, or local cache replay depending on customer tier
Create customer communication templates and product Console copy for incident states and recommended mitigations
decisions: Prioritize detecting and mitigating regional unavailability over transient token-latency spikes because enterprise SLAs require availability guarantees
Favor automated fallback chains with explicit quality-expectation labels rather than silent swaps (we will surface expected quality delta to customers)
Limit primary fallback candidates to models with validated prompt-compatibility and a measured <15% drop in task-specific quality on our eval sets
Use staged simulation (staging -> shadow -> limited production) for any automated routing change rather than broad rollout
